take: Brent capping its biggest weekly drop since the pandemic as the war premium unwinds is the dominant crude signal, and the EIA’s confirmation that US refineries ran above 95% of capacity from May to September—the highest since 1998—whilst shifting yields away from gasoline towards middle distillates tells you the complex is long distillate, not crude. The freight story is the one to respect: oil traders are lobbying Washington to release sanctioned tankers as a global vessel shortage pushes transportation costs to extraordinary levels, and with the shipbuilding orderbook up three and a half times since 2020 against only 30% yard capacity growth, the 2028 delivery crunch keeps tonne-miles and tanker earnings structurally bid even as flat price falls. The inventory angle cuts both ways—Venezuelan crude imports into the US hit 701,000 b/d in July, the most since 2017, before easing to 655,000 b/d in August, so heavy sour availability is improving just as ONGC negotiates to take over two Venezuelan projects within six months, which argues for further medium-heavy differential softening. Watch the gasoil-bunker spread as the transmission channel: distillate-led refinery yields plus expensive bunkers squeeze cracking economics, and any easing of sanctioned tonnage would hit freight first and product arb economics second. In the next 24 hours, track whether the tanker-release request gains any official traction, the first prints on post-midterm policy risk after the Democratic victory, and whether the crude sell-off extends into the weekly open or finds support from the still-elevated distillate margin structure.

items.title: LNG imports make up increasing share of Colombia's natural gas supply

Colombia's government has declared a national disaster in anticipation of a drought resulting from an expected strong El Niño.

items.title: U.S. refineries have been running at very high rates in 2026

Tight global product supplies this year have boosted margins for petroleum products, particularly for diesel, incentivizing the increased run rates.
